correctness.rationale: From Theorem 1.1 and A=p^(a+o(1)), B=p^(b+o(1)), C=p^(c+o(1)), the p-exponent of Δ1 is -(a+b)/(2r)-c/r+(r+1)/(4r²)+max(a-b,0)/(2r)+max(max(ka,b+c)+b+c-1-1/(2r),0)/(2r). Thus 2r ζ_r=S-1/2-1/(2r)-max(M-1-1/(2r),0). Its denominator is 2r>0. The exact identity H_r=1/2+max(1/(2r),M-1), descending to H_inf=1/2+max(0,M-1), proves necessity and sufficiency of S>H_inf for some fixed integer r. Choose r large to satisfy both ζ_r>0 and c>1/(2r), giving C>4p^(1/(2r)); ka<1,b+c<1,a>0 meet all remaining source size hypotheses for large p. At equality ζ_r≤0 for every r, and p^o(1) does not provide a fixed saving. All weights are bounded as stated. The anisotropic example yields ζ_4=1/320. Strict side conditions avoid constant-sensitive boundaries.

originality.rationale: Decisive PRIOR IMPLICATION, not a mere title overlap: arXiv:2610.01524v1 (Fouvry--Shparlinski--Xi, 2026), Theorem 1.1 pp. 2-3 and §3.2-3.3 pp. 11 already proves the full unequal-length bound for every fixed positive integer r, with the exact factor Δ1 used in the record. For power laws, taking base-p exponents gives 2r ζ_r=S-[1/2+1/(2r)+max(M-1-1/(2r),0)]=S-[1/2+max(1/(2r),M-1)]. Because the source permits arbitrarily large fixed r and c>0 ensures its size hypothesis, there is some r with ζ_r>0 if and only if S>1/2+max(0,M-1). Thus the proposed iff region is an elementary, logically entailed corollary of the published general bound, even though the authors explicitly work out only the equal-length slice in Corollary 1.2. The owner coverage criterion counts a corollary of an earlier stronger result as COVERED regardless of wording or whether the exact inequality is displayed. No originality PASS can follow solely from failure to locate the rearranged inequality in text search.
residual_risks: The 2026 theorem is source-strength evidence of coverage, not a claim that the authors explicitly wrote the three-exponent boundary; the distinction is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The unequal-parameter regime is naturally relevant to character-sum applications, and the inequality is a convenient phase-diagram summary, but no independent mathematical problem remains after using the published full unequal-range bound. The entire proposed contribution reduces to a routine power-exponent substitution and the one-line identity 1/(2r)+max(M-1-1/(2r),0)=max(1/(2r),M-1), followed by r→∞. No new sum estimate, nonstandard lemma, boundary phenomenon beyond the theorem, or independent classification problem is solved. The anisotropic example merely evaluates the already published inequality. Under the common value bar this is an expository corollary / routine re-expression rather than a substantively useful new mathematical fact, even though the explicit summary may help readers apply the antecedent.
residual_risks: The explicit statement may have expository utility as a compact guide to applications, which does not by itself supply independent research value.
No general or downstream theorem is demanded for value; the failure is that the entire exact formula is mechanically entailed by the stronger prior theorem, not merely narrow scope.
